transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because... well, I just feel like I'm always moving from one thing to the next. I can't really just sit idle. And they changed the setup at work recently, which has just made it a lot harder to hide, I guess.
Did you experience this same restlessness and difficulty sitting still when you were a child?

Yeah, I guess so. It's... it's been around long before this job change. Back in grade school, my teachers used to write on my report cards that I was bright, but... careless. Said I talked out of turn a lot. They always had to remind me to just stay with my work. So... yeah.

Do you often have trouble sustaining your focus on work tasks or long projects?

Yeah, I suppose so. Um... like when we have those longer coaching meetings, or... or if I have to read over a new procedure. I'll start off fine, but... after a few minutes, I realize my eyes are just moving across the page. I don't really take in what was said.
Have you ever experienced periods lasting several days where you had unusually high energy and needed much less sleep than usual without feeling tired?
No. I've always needed my sleep. Never had anything like that.
Do you find yourself constantly worrying about a lot of different everyday things, to the point where it feels difficult to control?
No... not really. I mean, I worry about normal things, I guess. But... it's not out of control or anything like that. Just the usual stuff.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits clinically significant symptoms of both inattention (trouble sustaining focus on tasks/reading, easily losing track) and hyperactivity/impulsivity (inability to sit idle, constantly moving from one thing to the next, interrupting coworkers before they finish speaking). Symptoms have been present since childhood (grade school reports of being careless, talking out of turn, needing reminders to stay on task) and cause functional impairment in the work setting. Mood and anxiety disorders were screened and ruled out.
